title: Online Safety Monitoring for LLMs
abstract: Despite alignment training, LLMs remain prone to generating unsafe outputs at deployment time. Monitoring outputs online and raising an alarm when safety can no longer be assumed is therefore critical. We study a simple real-time monitor that turns a verifier signal from an external model into an alarm decision by thresholding, with the threshold calibrated via risk control. In experiments on mathematical reasoning and red teaming datasets, we show that this simple design is competitive with more advanced monitors based on sequential hypothesis testing.

significance.justification: The paper introduces a practical safety monitoring approach that builders can implement to detect unsafe LLM outputs in real-time, addressing a critical deployment concern.

novelty.justification: While the risk control calibration approach is applied to safety monitoring, the core methodology builds on existing conformal prediction and sequential testing techniques.

reproducibility.justification: The method is clearly described with threshold calibration via risk control, but no mention of code or dataset availability is provided in the abstract.

clarity.justification: The abstract clearly states the problem, proposed solution, and experimental domains (mathematical reasoning and red teaming) with appropriate scope.

topical_fit.justification: Directly addresses LLM safety monitoring at deployment time, which is a core concern for engineers building production LLM systems.
